turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: What brings you here today?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I just had uh, well, it was just uh, I came from football practice I, uh, just felt like somebody fell on me while, like while I was on the ground and it's like, I've had this shoulder pain immediately afterwards and I can see a, like lump, um, kind of pointing out like in my skin here on my, on my, um, clavicle or shoulder bone.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, is it the right side or the left side?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, it's the right side.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: The right side, okay. Um, okay, and how long ago did this happen?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: It happened about, just a couple of hours ago. Yeah, just about 2 hours ago.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, um. Um, did someone, did someone fall onto your side? Okay, uh, so, your main, are you having mainly pain in that, in that area, or is it going to other places?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: It's mostly just the pain like right in that area. I'm not feeling it anywhere else.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, and um, what kind of pain are you feeling? Is it sharp, stabbing, or is it aching?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: It's really sharp. It feels like I'm, I'm getting stabbed in the shoulder.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, I see, and on a scale of 0 to 10, 10 being the worst pain you've felt in your life, how much would you rate it?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, this is like a 10. It hurts really bad.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, and um, are able to do any movements, or are you just kind of holding your arm up with your other other arm?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I, yeah I've just been holding my arm up by, uh, I kind of made a sling out of, yeah, like the coaches helped make a sling out of one of the, uh, what we, like a shirt or something like that at the practice. And so I've been just kind of holding my arm against my chest with my elbow flexed. I haven't really moved it at all.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: I see, okay. Um, and if you were to describe just what it looks like right now, does your shoulder kind of seem like it's sagging?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah it does.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, and do you notice any point near your shoulder like clavicle area that has any bruising, swelling looks, like red? Anything like that?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, like maybe a little bit of bruising and swelling like over the area where I can see like my, my skin pointing up, but um, yeah, that's the only area.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, I see. Okay. Any other symptoms, like any pain in any other joints, muscles?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, just the pain right there.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay. Alright um, and uh, other than that, have you previously had any popped joints before?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, I, no, I haven't.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, and no other trauma or anything in the same region?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I haven't had any pains there before or anything like that.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, I see. Okay, um and have you been diagnosed with any medical conditions in the past?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, no I haven't.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, alright, and did you hurt yourself anywhere else? Like did you hurt your head at all? Um, suffer any loss of consciousness or anything like that?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, no, I, I didn't. I was kind of just like laying on my side and they fell like on my left shoulder and I, I just got squished.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, and did it have any impact on your chest like you do you feel short of breath or anything like that?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No shortness of breath, kind of knocked the wind out of me at at first, but I'm okay now.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, I see, that's good. Um, okay, and other than uh, so no medical conditions? Do you take any medications at all?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, yeah, I'll take like uh, just some allergy medication every once in a while. When it's like, just seasonal allergies, I think to just some environmental triggers is all.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, and and do you have any allergies to any medications at all?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, no, I don't believe so.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, anything that you've tried that has helped or made your pain worse?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I haven't, I haven't taken anything yet, I just uh, like basically came right from practice to the, to the hospital.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, um, have you had any kind of fevers or chills?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Any skin changes, like rashes?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I haven't had any rashes.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, any weakness in your upper or lower extremities, besides like the area that's affected?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: No, okay. Um, any dizziness, fainting episodes?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, no, nothing like that.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, and your hearing and vision is alright right now?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: It is, yeah. I haven't had any problems with that.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, and have you had any kind of concussions or anything in the past?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, no, I haven't had any.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Alright. Uh, have you been hospitalized or had any surgeries in the past?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, no, not, not ever.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay. Any family history of any medical conditions?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, no. No, nothing that I can think of. Everybody's pretty healthy.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay. Um, and what's your living situation like right now?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: So I live with both of my parents and um, I have a younger brother and a younger sister as well. We live in a, in a house.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, alright, and um, do you work currently? Or are you a student?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, I'm in high school and, um, I, I work part-time at the grocery store as well, but uh, it's not that often though, because I've just been been playing sports, on the football team, we have a lot of practices and games and stuff.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay. Um, do you drink alcohol?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh I, sometimes I, with friends. Um, we've had a couple of beers here and, here and there, but I mean it's, it's not something that I've done very often. Yeah, we've been pretty safe, I feel like.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, and do you smoke cigarettes or marijuana, or use any recreational drugs?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, nothing like that.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, alright, so those are all the questions I had for you today. We'll do a full physical examination of the area. Um, we, we will definitely get an x-ray of the shoulder and clavicle to see what kind of, it seems like you have a clavicular fracture from just the mechanism of the injury, as well as everything you were describing. Um, but it is important to understand how, like what kind of clavicle injury it is and where it's affected, if it's in the middle area, on like the outer areas of the clavicle, um, and how much it's displaced because that will determine if we just need to reduce it here, and then give you a sling, and then you can go home. That's usually the case, but sometimes you may require surgery as well, and we would need to refer you to an orthopaedic surgeon. So yeah, we'll, we'll get the x-ray done, and if you need anything for pain currently, we will give you some medications here, um and then we'll go from there.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Alright, thank you.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: You're welcome. Um, I'll be here with you shortly.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: That sounds good. Thank you so much.
